fixture.note: Explicit density fixture adds normal enemies through spawnEnemy and preserves initial enemies, spawnClock, HP, speed, AI, damage and normal subsequent spawning. Existing Continue/preload/resume UI launches the memory-only checkpoint.

preparation.note: Original native texture submission and shader API readiness before launch; not GPU completion, measured FPS or first-draw validation. A maximum of three original enemy models is owned until adoption.

costs.note: QA measures synchronous CPU call wall time, including waits and observer overhead. Nested stage observations overlap and must not be summed. This is not GPU execution time, presented FPS, paint or total memory. First-observed owner identities are not game/model construction times. The observer performs no tick, render, pose, draw, pixel read, upload, event drain or scheduling calls.

native.note: QA instrumentation measures CPU call wall time only, including any synchronous wait and instrumentation overhead. It does not measure GPU execution, FPS or total memory. Stage fields are independent inclusive observations: nested stages overlap and must not be summed.

note: 8851 genuine-memory QA only. Fresh separation Map/buckets → pooled → fresh. Same normal60/180 checkpoint, AI/HP/automatic fire/spawning/offered upgrades, fixed .12s catch-up through actual advanceSimulation and pooled interpolation, 40renders/batch8/10warm excluded. Every arm owns a new original256 NPC rig with the same bounded three-model texture/shader preparation, excluded from combat timing, and primes the actual renderer without ticks before measurement. Main player/world caches can still vary. Allocation counters count the helper source objects, not heap/GC/RAM/VRAM bytes or all JavaScript allocations. No presented FPS, GPU execution or full product HUD/audio/save claim. Stage wrappers add overhead and nested call-wall times overlap. Original rig/resolution/materials/clips/positions/private outputs remain in use.
